page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-180 is an x86_64 general-purpose compute instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors. The instance provides 180 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 90 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading, alongside 720 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512 vector support (with AVX-512 VNNI and BF16), accelerated cryptography instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, and cache control mechanisms like CLWB and WBNOINVD. The instance does not include integrated GPUs, bundled local NVMe storage, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external block storage and cloud networking configurations for persistence and external access.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional parallel processing and memory throughput. The server achieved top-decile performance across multi-core compute tests, including a multi-core stress-ng score of 277,209.33 and a PassMark CPU score of 123,447.51. In memory-intensive evaluations, uncached read bandwidth reached 356.6 GB/sec, supporting high throughput in data-handling scenarios such as Redis SET operations, which logged 211.43 million operations per second. Multi-threaded Clang compilation and ray tracing also scored in the top tier. While single-threaded compression and multi-threaded decompression tests demonstrated mid-tier execution speeds, prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and large language model evaluations scored in the top decile for CPU-based inference.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the c3d-standard-180 provides dense CPU and memory allocation suitable for organizations consolidating horizontal workloads into a single large system. The lack of onboard local storage represents a potential I/O tradeoff, shifting disk-intensive reliance entirely to attached cloud volumes. This instance profile is engineered for CPU-heavy enterprise workloads, large in-memory databases, continuous integration build clusters, batch data processing, and large-scale web serving tiers.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-180 is a general-purpose cloud instance featuring 180 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor and 720 GB of RAM. Based on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions, it maintains a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration omits local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on attached network storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier multi-core computing capability and memory throughput, demonstrated by exceptional scores in multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and Redis operations exceeding 211 million operations per second. CPU-based LLM inference and heavy software compilation also perform at the top decile. The platform is structured for large-scale enterprise applications, high-concurrency in-memory data caching, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and parallel batch processing.
